title: SKF India (Industrial) Ltd - 544572 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: SKF India (Industrial) Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.3% YoY to INR 9,708 mn, but PBT margin fell to ~9% on FX losses and demerger IT costs.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was INR 9,708 million, up 18.3% YoY (on management's constructed comparison) and 2.6% QoQ. PBT was INR 869 million, a margin of about 9%, hit by roughly INR 147 million of forex loss and about INR 150 million of demerger-related IT separation cost. Operating cash conversion was 63%, with a one-time outflow for name change and land transfer. Management reiterated a long-term PBT margin path of 14-16% through 2028, with a 17-19% aspiration, and a new Pune plant with INR 850-950 crore capex targeted for 2028.

financial_highlights.change: Down QoQ due to forex and demerger one-offs
Rupee depreciation, linked to Middle East war; on imports mainly from Europe
Incremental one-time cost in the quarter
Operating cash flow hit by name-change and land-transfer charges

segments.name: General machinery (pumps, motors, gears)
segments.commentary: Management called general machinery the strongest segment this quarter and said its share of business has grown.

segments.name: Wind and heavy industry
segments.commentary: Named as other strong performers in the quarter; rail described as solid.

segments.name: Distribution channel
segments.commentary: Highest-margin channel; management cited high double-digit margins versus high single-digit for OE.

segments.name: OE channel
segments.commentary: About 54% of revenue; lower margin but supports aftermarket share growth.

segments.name: Solutions (services, remanufacturing, condition monitoring)
segments.commentary: Around 6-7% of India business, below 10%; being scaled with added technology and direct sales staff.

guidance_outlook: Long-term PBT margin guidance of 14-16%, described as conservative; aspiration 17-19%, with near-term pressure from investments through 2028.
Management expects demerger IT costs to continue for two more quarters, tapering by end-2026 and ceasing around Q4/Q1 FY28.
Management said ~12% is a fair margin on current performance excluding the one-offs; manufacturing efficiency could add a couple of percentage points more.
Aspiration to double the India Industrial business in about five years, with no firm timeline committed.
Pune plant (capex INR 850-950 crore; 900-950 in one remark) expected to start production in 2028, with payback of 5-7 years including channel transfers and new third-party and SKF group channels.
Sujeeth Pai to succeed Mukund Vasudevan as MD effective 1 September 2026.
capex_capacity: New Pune factory is the key constraint: majority of new channel installations are tied to the factory coming online in 2028; capacity is currently constrained by space, not demand.
New tapered roller bearing (TRB) line in Pune adds 3 million units annually, serving agriculture, gearbox and aftermarket; supports exports too.
One additional TRB channel to be added by early 2027 despite capacity constraints.
Plan to add around 15-20 lines, some transferred from SKF group companies and some new; most depend on the new factory.
Capex plan quoted as INR 900-950 crore in prepared remarks and INR 850-900 crore in later Q&A; figures are inconsistent in the transcript.
demand_pricing: Order book reported as growing, with sustained growth over the last few quarters.
INR 140 crore gearbox-manufacturer order (wind-related, one-year, spread through the year) and INR 35 crore agricultural tractor OEM contract.
Innovation traction strongest in general machinery (gearboxes, motors, pumps); agriculture uses customised offerings.
Data center and humanoid opportunities are early-stage; current data center traction is in basic pumps, with no material revenue yet.
Management said the Indian Automotive sales share is being reduced to improve mix.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the margin moderation from the 16-19% guidance to 14-16%, and how much is FX and demerger impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 14-16% is the conservative long-term path and 17-19% the aspiration; near-term margins dip due to investments. CFO quantified FX plus demerger one-offs at about 3% of margin, implying ~12% underlying.

qa_highlights.question: What is the supply and recurrence profile of the INR 140 crore wind and INR 35 crore agri orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Most orders are one-time or one-year contracts, typically extending one to two years. Some services and condition-monitoring contracts are longer-term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin difference across distribution, OE and exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Distribution is the higher-margin channel at high double-digit margins; OE is high single-digit. OE supports aftermarket share growth.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the solutions business and what is the doubling timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Solutions are around 6-7% of India business, below 10% in aspiration. Doubling the business is an aspiration within five years at the outside, with no committed timeline.

qa_highlights.question: When will one-off costs end, and is 12% margin achievable now?
qa_highlights.answer: The IT cost should taper through end-2026 and stop around Q4 FY27/Q1 FY28. CFO said ~12% is a fair current margin, with further gains from efficiency and the Pune plant.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company merge with the SKF automotive or other group entities?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no active plans; it wants the demerger to stabilise first but continuously evaluates options.

risks_watch: Forex: rupee depreciation linked to Middle East tensions raised import costs on European-sourced products; margin impact depends on INR movement.
Demerger one-offs: IT separation costs of about INR 150 million per quarter expected for two more quarters; watch for taper.
Capacity constraint until the 2028 Pune plant; growth above current capacity is limited, with only one added TRB channel by early 2027.
Execution risk on INR 850-950 crore capex and the 5-7 year payback; management figures varied across the call.
Management transition: Sujeeth Pai takes over as MD on 1 September 2026.
Data disclosure: prior-year comparison is based on management assumptions and carve-out financials, not reported comparatives.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, tailwinds and order momentum, but cautious on near-term margins, which management tied to FX and demerger costs. Answers on the margin path and capex figures were somewhat inconsistent, and the call had audio interruptions.
key_quotes: So our revenue from operations was INR9,708 million for the quarter.
We are trying to bring down the India Automotive sales to ensure our mix improves further.
So putting the entire investment together, we are looking at a payback between five to seven years.

adds.what: New tapered roller bearing (TRB) line in Pune adding 3 million units annually
One additional TRB channel to be added in Pune
New Pune factory (state-of-the-art), expected to start production in 2028
15-20 new production lines, some transferred from SKF group companies and some new, mostly dependent on the new Pune factory

growth.why: Management gives no explicit revenue growth guidance; Q1 revenue rose 18.3% YoY, and growth is backed partly by a new Pune TRB line (3 mn units/yr, live now), one more TRB channel by early 2027, and a 2028 Pune factory (INR 850-950 cr) with 15-20 lines, though most new capacity depends on the 2028 factory and the doubling-in-five-years aspiration has no firm timeline.

mgmt.note: Sujeeth Pai succeeds Mukund Vasudevan as MD effective 1 September 2026; no specific growth plan detailed beyond the Pune factory and doubling aspiration.
initiatives: Aspiration to double India Industrial business in about five years
